Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:1.english: And do you think - that here, the reed that the Rabbis required of him is so that it will not be erased?

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:2.english: What are the circumstances of this reed - [that is placed] to protect it.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:3.hebrew: אי דמיהדק - שלא יכנסו בו מים וימחק, הוי חציצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:3.english: If [it is] firmly attached - So that water will not enter it and [the Name] be erased, it is an interposition.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:4.english: And if it is not firmly attached - to his flesh.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:5.english: The water enters it - and it does not protect [the Name] from being erased.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:6.hebrew: תיפוק ליה דמשום דיו - בלא גמי נמי חייץ דיו. ומשני: בלחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:6.english: Derive that [it is] due to [the] ink - Even without [a] reed, [the] ink also interposes. And [the Gemara] answers: [When it is] moist.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:13:7.english: Nevertheless, [it is] difficult - Why do the Rabbis [need] a reed?

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:14:1.hebrew: מכלל דלר' יוסי כו' - בתמיה, והא כתיב "לא יראה בך ערות דבר" (דברים כ״ג:ט״ו):
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:14:1.english: [Is that to say] by inference that according to Rabbi Yosei, etc. - [This is asked] in astonishment: Is it not written, "that He see no unseemly thing in you" (Deuteronomy 23:15)?

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:15:1.hebrew: אלא אי איכא גמי הכי נמי - דמודה ר' יוסי דצריך לכרוך עליו גמי, ולא סגי ליה לאנוחי ידיו עליו, דילמא מישתלי ושקיל ליה לידיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:15:1.english: Rather, if there is a reed, [it is] indeed so - For Rabbi Yosei concedes that one must wrap a reed around it, and it is not sufficient for him to place his hands upon it, lest he forget and remove his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:1:1.hebrew: הוא דאמר כר"ש - דשרי לעכובי דליקה בעור גדי:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:1:1.english: He said [his ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - Who permits holding back a fire with the hide of a kid.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:2:1.hebrew: גרם כיבוי - כי האי גוונא, כשמגיע למים הוא כבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:2:1.english: Indirectly causing extinguishing - In such a case, when [the fire] reaches the water, it is extinguished.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:2:2.hebrew: מי אמר - דילמא הא דקתני במתני', ״ועושין מחיצה בכל הכלים״, לאו בחדשים המתבקעים קאמר:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:2:2.english: Did he say [so] - Perhaps that which is taught in the Mishnah, "and they may make a partition with any vessels," is not speaking of new [vessels] that burst.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:3:1.english: A candle - [That is] lit; [in Old French:] croisel [an oil lamp].

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:3:2.english: Only where one forgot - That he forgot it while it was still day on the board, unintentionally.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:3:3.hebrew: אבל מניח נעשית - טבלא בסיס לדבר האסור, ואסור לטלטלה כדי לנערה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:3:3.english: However, [where] one places [it], [it] becomes - [the] board [becomes] a base for a forbidden object, and it is forbidden to move it in order to shake it.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:4:1.english: He would curse it - Against all who rule thus.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:4:2.hebrew: כר' יהודה - דאמר דבר שאין מתכוין אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:4:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - Who says [that] an unintentional act is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:5:1.english: In [a case of] "Cut off its head" - And here too, the wind extinguishes it.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:6:1.hebrew: כנגד המדורה - ואע"פ שרוח מנשבת ומבעיר האור:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:6:1.english: Opposite the fire - Even though a wind is blowing and kindling the fire.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:6:2.hebrew: מאי טעמא דמאן דאסר - אין דרך להבעיר ברוח מצויה, ולא פסיק רישיה ולא ימות הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:6:2.english: What is the reason of the one who prohibits - It is not normal to kindle [a fire] with a typical wind, and it is not [a case of] pesik reishei ve-lo yamut [an inevitable consequence].

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:1.hebrew: אף כלי כפר שיחין - חרס העשוי מאותו עפר, חזק הוא ואין משתבר. אלמא לר' יוסי, בגרם כבוי טפי מיקל מדרבנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:1.english: Even vessels of Kfar Shiḥin - Earthenware made from that soil is strong and does not break. Thus, according to Rabbi Yosei, [he] is more lenient regarding indirect extinguishing than the Rabbis.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:2.hebrew: וכי תימא איפוך מתני' - ותני ברישא דברי ר' יוסי, וחכמים אוסרין בכלי חרס חדשים כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:2.english: And if you say: Reverse the mishna - And teach in the first clause: "[These are] the words of Rabbi Yosei, and the Sages prohibit [using] new earthenware vessels," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:3.hebrew: ור' יוסי דברייתא - דמשמע דבהנהו דפקעי מודה, דהא כפר שיחין וכפר חנניה הוא דקשרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:3.english: And Rabbi Yosei of the baraita - Which implies that regarding those [vessels] that burst he concedes [that they are prohibited], for it is [only vessels of] Kefar Shichin and Kefar Chananya that he permits.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:4.hebrew: לדבריהם קאמר להו - לדידי כל הכלים שרו, דגרם כבוי מותר. אלא לדידכו, נהי דאסריתו גרם כבוי, אודו לי מיהת דבהני אפילו גרם ליכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:7:4.english: He is speaking to them according to their view - According to me, all vessels are permitted, for indirect extinguishing is permitted. Rather, according to you, even though you prohibit indirect extinguishing, concede to me at least that with these [vessels] there is not even indirect [extinguishing].

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:9:1.hebrew: כורך עליו גמי - קס"ד השתא כדי שלא ימחק את השם במים. אלמא לרבנן גרם מחק אסור, ולר' יוסי שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 120b:9:1.english: He wraps a reed over it - [The Gemara] currently assumes [that he does this] so that he will not erase the [divine] Name in the water. Thus, according to the Rabbis, indirectly causing erasure is prohibited, and according to Rabbi Yosei it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 120b:9:2.english: Provided that he does not rub - For [that] is erasing directly.

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:12:1.hebrew: אי הכי קשה דרבנן אדרבנן - בלאו הכי הוה קשיא דרבנן אדרבנן, אלא משום דהשתא פריך מכ"ש, קאמר "אי הכי":
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:12:1.english: If so, there is a contradiction between [one statement of] the Rabbis and [another statement of] the Rabbis - Even without this, there would be a contradiction between [the two statements of] the Rabbis; rather, because [the Gemara] now asks from [an argument of] "all the more so," it says "if so."

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:2:1.hebrew: גרם כיבוי מי אמר - וא"ת: הא קתני מתני' בין מלאים בין ריקנים, ומאי רבותא איכא טפי במלאים מבריקנים אי לאו דמיירי בדרכן להשתבר? וי"ל: דס"ד דמיירי בכלים שאין דרכן להשתבר, וקמ"ל דלא גזרינן אטו כלים שדרכן להשתבר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:2:1.english: "Did he say [it is permitted to] indirectly cause extinguishing?" - And if you ask: Doesn't the Mishnah teach "whether full or empty," and what greater novelty is there in [permitting] full ones than empty ones, if not that it is speaking of [vessels] whose nature is to burst? And one can answer: that you might have thought it is speaking of vessels whose nature is not to burst, and [the Mishnah] teaches us that we do not decree [a prohibition against them] on account of vessels whose nature is to burst.

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:3:1.hebrew: מנער את הטבלא והיא נופלת ואם כבתה כבתה - אומר ר"י דמיירי דליכא שמן בנר, דאי איכא שמן בנר חייב, שהרי שופך ממנו והוי כמסתפק ממנו דחייב משום מכבה, כדאמר בפ"ב דביצה (דף כב:). ובירושלמי מוקי לה בנר שכבה, ולא קתני בהך ברייתא "ואם כבתה כבתה", ואתא לאשמעינן היתר טלטול ע"י ניעור לר' יהודה, דאסר טלטול בנר שכבה; אי נמי אפילו לר"ש, ובנר גדול כגון קערה ועששית דמודה ר"ש, כדאמר בפרק [כירה] (דף מד.), או כשיש אפר וגחלת אלא שכבה השלהבת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:3:1.english: One shakes the board and it falls, and if it is extinguished, it is extinguished - Ri says that [this] refers to where there is no oil in the lamp, for if there is oil in the lamp, one is liable, since he pours [oil] from it, and it is like drawing [oil] from [a burning lamp], for which one is liable on account of extinguishing, as stated in the second chapter of Beitzah (22b). And in the Jerusalem [Talmud], it establishes [the baraita] as referring to a lamp that has gone out, and in that baraita it does not teach "and if it is extinguished, it is extinguished," and it comes to teach us the permissibility of moving [it] by means of shaking according to Rabbi Yehudah, who prohibits moving a lamp that has gone out; alternatively, [it applies] even according to Rabbi Shimon, in the case of a large lamp such as a dish or a lantern, where Rabbi Shimon concedes [that it is muktzeh], as stated in chapter [Keirah] (44a), or when there are ashes and embers, except that the flame has gone out.

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:4:1.hebrew: פותח ונועל כדרכו - אע"פ שע"י כן מתנדנד הנר, ומתרחק השמן מן השלהבת או מתקרב, והוי מכבה או מבעיר. אבל אין לפרש משום כיבוי דרוח, דאחורי הדלת ליכא רוח. ועוד, דא"כ הוה ליה למימר: "פותח אדם דלת כנגד הנר", כדקאמר בסמוך: "כנגד המדורה". ועוד: דתינח פותח — נועל מאי איסורא איכא? אלא כדפרישית. ואי לאו משום כיבוי והבערה, משום טלטול אין לאסור, דבנעילת דלת לא חשיב טלטול, וגם לא הוי בסיס לדבר האסור, דבית חשוב הוא ובטל אגב בית; אי נמי בשכח, דלא הוי בסיס:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:4:1.english: One may open and shut [the door] in his [usual] manner - Even though thereby the lamp sways and the oil moves away from the flame or draws closer, and it is [a case of] extinguishing or kindling. However, one should not explain [that the concern is] because of extinguishing by wind, because behind the door there is no wind. And furthermore, if so, it should have said, "A person opens a door opposite the lamp," just as it says nearby, "opposite the bonfire." And furthermore: this suffices for "opens" — [as for] "shuts," what prohibition is there? Rather, [it is] as I explained. And if not for [the concern of] extinguishing and kindling, one could not prohibit [it] on account of moving [a muktzeh object], because through shutting the door it is not considered moving [the lamp], and also [the door] does not become a base for a forbidden object, because the house is significant and [the lamp] is nullified relative to the house; or else [it refers to a case] where he forgot [the lamp there], in which case it does not become a base.

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:6:1.hebrew: מר סבר גזרינן - הלכך צריך ליזהר שלא לפתוח הדלת לפני המדורה אפילו ברוח מצויה, דהא לייט עלה אביי דהוי בתראה. והנ"מ כשהמדורה קצת קרובה אצל הדלת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:6:1.english: One Sage holds that we issue a decree - Therefore, one must be careful not to open the door in front of the fire even in a typical wind, since Abaye, who is the later [authority], cursed [anyone who does] so. And this applies [only] when the fire is somewhat close to the door:

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:7:1.hebrew: והא איפכא שמעינן להו - לאו דווקא איפכא, דר' יוסי דברייתא הוי כמו מתני' דאסר דרכו להשתבר; אלא היינו איפכא: דבמתניתין מחמיר ר' יוסי טפי מדרבנן, ובברייתא מיקל טפי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:7:1.english: "Didn't we hear them [state] the opposite?" - Not literally the opposite, for Rabbi Yosei of the baraita is like [Rabbi Yosei of] the Mishnah, who prohibits [using a vessel whose] nature is to break; rather, this is [the sense in which it is] the opposite: that in the Mishnah Rabbi Yosei is more stringent than the Rabbis, whereas in the baraita he is more lenient [than they are].

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:7:2.hebrew: וכי תימא איפוך מתני' כו' - וא"ת: מ"מ תקשה, דבמתני' לא אסרי רבנן אלא חרס חדש, ובברייתא אסרי אפי' ישן, מדנקט כלי מתכות? וי"ל: דנקט בברייתא כלי מתכות משום דאין חילוק בהם בין חדשים לישנים, וה"ה כלי חרס ישן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:7:2.english: And if you say: Reverse the Mishnah, etc. - And if you ask: In any case, it is [still] difficult, for in the Mishnah the Rabbis only prohibit new earthenware, whereas in the baraita they prohibit even old [earthenware], since [it] specifies metal vessels? And one can answer: [The baraita] specifies metal vessels because there is no distinction among them between new and old, and the same applies to an old earthenware vessel.

Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:7:3.hebrew: והאמר רבה כו' - ואם תאמר: ואמאי לא מפיך ברייתא, דטפי אית לן לאפוכה ממתני', והוי אתי נמי שפיר הא דרבה בר תחליפא, ונימא דרבנן לדברי ר' יוסי קאמרי, ואינהו שרי אף בכלי חרס חדש? וי"ל: דהתלמוד לא קאמר אלא דאפילו מפיך מתני' לא אתי שפיר, אלא על כרחיך ברייתא אית לן לתרוצי; וכיון דאתינא להכי, לא צריך להפוכה, אלא למימר חסורי מיחסרא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120b:7:3.english: "Didn't Rabbah say, etc." - And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not reverse the baraita, as we have more reason to reverse it than the Mishnah, and this [statement] of Rabbah bar Taḥalifa would also fit well, and we would say that the Rabbis [in the baraita] are speaking according to the view of Rabbi Yosei, while they themselves permit even new earthenware vessels? One can say: The Talmud is only saying that even if you reverse the Mishnah, it does not work out well; rather, perforce we must resolve the baraita. And since we have arrived at this [conclusion], it is not necessary to reverse it, but rather to say [that the baraita is] chasorei mechassera [i.e., missing words].
